Definition: properly, a creaking (or shrill sound), i.e. shout (of joy or grief)
BiblicalUsage: When the text says rinnâh, it means a creaking (or shrill sound), that is shout (of joy or grief). In 1 Kings 8:28, we read, "…his supplication, O LORD my God, to hearken…"; in 2 Chronicles 6:19, "…his supplication, O LORD my God, to hearken…". You hear it again in Isaiah 14:7 — "…rest, is quiet: they break forth into singing" — and in Jeremiah 7:16, "…this people, neither lift up cry nor prayer…".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe rinnâh matters because God chose this word, and it tells the truth about how God deals with his people. I believe rinnâh is still true for us, because the God who gave it has not changed his mind.
